trial_court: Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Hamirpur, H.P. (Cr. Revision No. 304 of 2023)
case_name: Naresh Kumar vs Surekha And Another

parties.respondent_defendant: Surekha and another — wife and child

facts_of_case: The respondent filed an application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. for grant of maintenance @ ₹10,000/- per month to each of the applicants. The relationship between the parties remained cordial for 5-6 months of the marriage. The respondent went to Dubai to earn his livelihood and remained in Dubai till 2007.

legal_principles.principle: The higher court does not sit as a regular court of appeal. Its function is to ensure that law is being properly administered.
legal_principles.held: Such a court cannot embark upon the fruitless task of determining the issues by reappreciating the evidence.
cited_cases: Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander, (2012) 9 SCC 460

legal_principles.principle: The revisional jurisdiction can be invoked where the decisions under challenge are grossly erroneous, there is no compliance with the provisions of law, the finding recorded is based on no evidence, material evidence is ignored or judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or perversely.
legal_principles.held: These are not exhaustive classes but are merely indicative. Each case would have to be determined on its own merits.
cited_cases: Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander, (2012) 9 SCC 460

legal_principles.principle: Where the testimony of a witness is not challenged in cross-examination, it cannot be challenged during arguments.
legal_principles.held: This position was reiterated in Arvind Singh v. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 11 SCC 1.
cited_cases: Arvind Singh v. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 11 SCC 1

outcome.final_order: Maintenance at the rate of ₹3,000/- per month each was awarded to each of the applicants from the date of filing of the petition.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for maintenance under Section 125 CrPC
responding to a revision petition in a family court case
advising on divorce and alimony matters
